standard_prerequisites.name: Rational rotation group and its halves
standard_prerequisites.statement: R is the group of rotations about the origin by rational radian values in [0, 2pi); the unit's disjoint-group lemma partitions R into R_1 (rational radians in [0, pi)) and R_2 = R \ R_1 such that the squares of the elements of either half exhaust R, the map theta to 2 theta being a bijection from [0, pi) to [0, 2pi).
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the two index sets and the reassembly identity {(rho composed with rho) : rho in R_i} = R (1042-1046, 1056-1062).

standard_prerequisites.name: Choice set for the circle
standard_prerequisites.statement: C is a set containing exactly one member from each equivalence class of the circle under the relation of differing by a rotation in R, obtained by Choice.
standard_prerequisites.use: The pieces of the partition are the images rho(C) (1046-1049).

standard_prerequisites.name: Cover and no-overlap lemmas
standard_prerequisites.statement: The unit's lemmas: the circle is the union of rho(C) over all rho in R, and distinct rotations give disjoint images of C.
standard_prerequisites.use: They establish that D_1 and D_2 partition the circle into pairwise disjoint pieces (1049-1053).

core_obligations: Define D_1 = union over R_1 of rho(C) and D_2 = union over R_2 of rho(C) (1044-1049).
By the cover and no-overlap lemmas the images rho(C) over all of R are pairwise disjoint and cover the circle, so D_1 and D_2 are disjoint and their union is the circle (1049-1053).
Each D_i is partitioned into the countably many pieces rho(C), rho in R_i, since R is countable (1053-1055).

Rotating each piece rho(C) by rho gives (rho composed with rho)(C); since squaring bijects R_i onto R, these rotated pieces are pairwise disjoint and their union is the circle, a copy of S^1; the same holds for D_2 (1055-1063).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the two unions over the group halves.
Invoke cover and no-overlap for the partition; count the pieces.
Reassemble each family into a copy of the circle via the squaring bijection.

difficulty_reason: The counted lemma is the author lemma at source lines 1036-1040: the circle admits a partition into two disjoint sets, each of which partitions into countably many pieces that can be rotated to form a copy of the circle. The author proof (1042-1063) is a complete construction in three cited steps: split the rational rotation group into halves R_1 and R_2 as in the unit's disjoint-group lemma, define D_i as the union of the choice-set images rho(C) over R_i; the images form a partition of the circle with disjoint pieces by the unit's cover and no-overlap lemmas; and each family can be rotated to a copy of the circle because squaring maps R_i onto the whole rotation group (the disjoint-group lemma's content: theta maps to 2 theta is a bijection from the half-range onto the full range), so rotating each piece rho(C) by rho yields the family {(rho composed with rho)(C)} whose union is the circle by the cover lemma. The construction, the partition argument, and the reassembly identity are all present; the invoked lemmas are proved earlier in the same unit.
